recap_lines: Two thresholds, on and off, give hysteresis and stop a state flickering.
A selector is or with priority, and a sequence is and with order.
Utility AI scores every option now, while GOAP searches for a plan.
A reward is one step's number, and the return adds them up over time.
The same seed gives the same output, and a validator rejects levels that fail.
Authority says who may change a value, and replication copies it to others.
bookends.command: Quiz me on game AI terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use hysteresis, flicker, selector, sequence, utility AI, GOAP, reward, generate-and-test, constructive generation and authority. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a small game situation, and the answer waits for you.

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Newcomers often think one distance is enough to make a guard start and stop chasing. It is not. With one threshold, a player at the edge makes the guard flicker. Two thresholds, one to start and a larger one to stop, give hysteresis. Game AI is full of pairs like that. This film goes through the terms group by group, each one shown.

For example, the Walker guard's lose radius is set larger than its sight radius, so a player hovering at the edge does not make it flicker.

beats.narration_text: A Selector, also called a fallback, tries its children in order and stops at the first one that does not fail. It is or, with priority. In the top row the first child fails, the second succeeds, and the third is skipped. If every child fails, the Selector fails, and if one is running, so is the Selector. For example, a guard's root Selector says chase if you can, else search, else patrol.
